subject: Post-call qualification: concurrency, streaming SLAs, regional routing & data sovereignty
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Eve Tan <eve.tan@acuitybio.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call qualification: concurrency, streaming SLAs, regional routing & data sovereignty

Eve / Acuity team — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive: 

Summary of requirements (from today's call):
- Latency: p95 generation target <= 180ms for short prompts (~32 tokens); p95 <= 350ms for long prompts (~512 tokens) when routed to dedicated capacity.
- Throughput: steady-state 800 requests/sec across the product, with ability to burst to 2,000 rps for traffic spikes (burst window ~5 minutes).
- Concurrency & streaming: conversational workloads expect 8–12 concurrent streams per user session; real-time streaming is required for the live-assist UI (token-by-token).
- Regional routing: EU customers must be served from EU region endpoints; APAC users prefer Singapore region but US origin acceptable where latency < 200ms to user.
- Data residency: training telemetry and logs for EU accounts must be stored and retained in EU only; non-PII request metadata can be replicated for debugging if customer-approved.

Open clarification items (action items):
1) Can you confirm the distribution of traffic by region (approx % US / EU / APAC)? this affects routing topology and cache warm-up strategy.
2) For streaming: are you using server-side aggregations or strictly client token streaming? helps decide batching vs low-latency path.
3) Data retention: confirm which artifacts (raw request bodies, KV caches, logs) must be restricted to EU.

Next steps (proposed):
- Marissa/Rafael to run a quick feasibility on a Dedicated pool configuration (NVIDIA H100 equivalent) that can meet 800 rps steady + 2k burst with streaming enabled. ETA: 48 hours.
- Acuity to share traffic split and example payload sizes (average tokens in/out).
- Karthik to send a short checklist for data sovereignty + IP ranges for firewall allowlist.
- Schedule technical deep-dive the week of Jul 12 to validate SLOs and test a small pilot.

Attachments: I attached a concise performance matrix (redwood-performance-matrix.csv) and a draft checklist for data-locality (acuity-data-sovereignty-checklist.pdf).

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Eve Tan <eve.tan@acuitybio.com>

Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 11:03:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Post-call qualification: concurrency, streaming SLAs, regional routing & data sovereignty

Thanks Karthik — good write-up. A few clarifications from our end: 

Traffic split (approx): US 55%, EU 30%, APAC 15%.
Payloads: typical prompt ~ 60 tokens, responses ~ 120 tokens; some bulk batch jobs produce 2–3k token outputs but those are non-interactive.
Streaming: client expects token-by-token streaming for the live-assist UI (no server-side aggregation) — low latency is primary. We will need an SDK hook to rehydrate partial responses for UI rendering.
Data residency: For EU customers we must ensure request payload and logs are stored in EU for the entire retention window (90 days). We can allow non-sensitive telemetry (e.g., model selection metrics) to be replicated out of region for infra debugging if encrypted and access-controlled.

Also: can you confirm whether Redwood supports regional routing with deterministic residency (i.e., requests from an EU account always hit EU-only endpoints even if that adds ~40–60ms latency)? There are contractual clauses around data locality that our legal/compliance team will enforce.

Happy to schedule the deep-dive on Jul 13–14; Jul 13 afternoon PDT works for us.

—Eve
Eve Tan
Director, Platform Engineering | Acuity Bio
eve.tan@acuitybio.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Eve Tan <eve.tan@acuitybio.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call qualification: concurrency, streaming SLAs, regional routing & data sovereignty

Eve — appreciate the specifics. Quick notes from engineering scoping (preliminary):

- Concurrency/throughput: a Dedicated pool with mixed-instance scaling (baseline nodes + burst nodes) will cover the steady 800 rps and 2k burst. We'll include continuous batching disabled on streaming routes to keep per-token latency low; streaming will use the low-latency exec path.
- Deterministic regional routing: supported via account-routing policies and can be enforced at the control plane level so EU accounts are pinned to EU-only serving clusters. That will add a predictable latency delta; we can quantify after we see region-to-region delta samples.
- Data residency controls: we support customer-managed retention gates and can disable cross-region log replication for specific tenants. We will need your compliance team to sign the DPA addendum that lists exactly which artifacts are restricted.

Attachments: redwood-performance-matrix.csv (bandwidth, token pricing, recommended pool sizes) included.

Action items we own:
- Rafael to produce a capacity sketch and estimated cost delta for EU-pinned routing vs global fallback (ETA: 48 hrs).
- Karthik to share allowlist IPs and a short DPA excerpt for Acuity legal.

Marissa
Marissa Cole

Eve — thanks for confirming the split and streaming behavior. Confirming the plan and next calendar items: 

1) Deep-dive: Jul 13, 09:30 PDT / Jul 13, 16:30 CET — invite sent. Please confirm attendee list.
2) Rafael will post the capacity sketch during the deep-dive; Marissa will present the low-latency streaming configuration.
3) I attached the quick allowlist (IPs + ports) and a redlined DPA excerpt to the shared Drive link. If your legal wants the DPA in DocuSign we can route it through our legal ops.
4) Pilot suggestion: 2-week dedicated pilot focused on EU-pinned routing for a subset of accounts (10–20% of EU traffic) so we can measure p95 delta and cache-hit curves. If acceptable, we'll provide a scoped pricing estimate.

Please reply with confirmation on the pilot and any additional stakeholders (legal/compliance) to include.

Best — Karthik
